title: The Sun, Moon and Stars
seo_title: Primary 1 Basic Science: The Sun, Moon and Stars Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 1 Basic Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: The Sun, the Moon and the stars are objects in the sky. The Sun gives light and heat; the Moon reflects sunlight and seems to change shape; the stars are far away and are seen at night. The Earth's rotation causes day and night. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 1, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): day and night, the Sun in the sky, the Moon, stars and watching the sky. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The Sun gives us light and heat.
key_sub: The Moon reflects light from the Sun.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Sun is a star, a huge ball of hot gas. It gives the Earth light and heat. The Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west because the Earth turns (rotates).

The Moon does not make its own light; it reflects sunlight. Its shape seems to change during a month. At night we can see many stars; they look tiny because they are very far away.

Example

Where does the Sun rise?

Morning side

Answer: in the east

Example

Why can we see the Moon?

It is not a light source.

Answer: it reflects sunlight

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun moves around the Earth.
  • Thinking the Moon gives off its own light.
  • Looking straight at the Sun.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the new moon?
items.e: The order is new moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent.

items.q: Why can we see the Moon?
c: It reflects light from the Sun.
It reflects light from the Earth's cities.
items.e: The Moon is not a light source.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the waxing crescent?
items.e: Waxing means growing; waning means shrinking.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes after the last quarter?
items.e: New → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → last quarter → waning crescent.

items.q: What happens in a solar eclipse?
c: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks the Sun.
Earth blocks sunlight from the Moon.
items.e: Solar eclipses happen at new moon.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the waning gibbous?
items.e: Waxing means growing; waning means shrinking.

items.q: What causes day and night?
c: the Earth spinning on its axis
items.e: One spin takes about 24 hours.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the waning crescent?
items.e: Waxing means growing; waning means shrinking.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the last quarter?
items.e: The order is new moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent.

items.q: What causes the phases of the Moon?
c: We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it orbits the Earth.
items.e: Half is always lit.

items.q: How long does the Moon take to orbit Earth?
c: about 27 days (and about 29.5 days from one new moon to the next)
items.e: This is roughly a month.

items.q: Why does the Moon seem to change shape?
c: We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth.
items.e: Half the Moon is always lit by the Sun.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes after the waxing crescent?
items.e: New → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → last quarter → waning crescent.

items.q: What is a full moon?
c: when we see the whole sunlit side of the Moon
items.e: Earth is between the Sun and Moon.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the waxing gibbous?
items.e: The order is new moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes after the waning crescent?
items.e: The order is new moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent.

items.q: What causes the seasons?
c: Earth's tilted axis as it orbits the Sun
items.e: The tilt changes how directly sunlight reaches each place.

items.q: Why should you never look straight at a solar eclipse?
c: The Sun's light can permanently damage your eyes.
items.e: Use eclipse glasses or a pinhole viewer.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes after the waxing gibbous?

items.q: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon?
c: The other side is dark rock.
It spins once in the same time it takes to orbit the Earth.
items.e: The far side is not always dark.
